theory.intro: **Scalar multiplication** multiplies a vector by a number $k$. The new vector is parallel to the original: it is $|k|$ times as long, and it points the opposite way when $k$ is negative.
facts: In column form, multiply each component by $k$, so $3\begin{pmatrix}2\\-5\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-15\end{pmatrix}$.
The length scales by the size of $k$: $\left|k\underset{\sim}{a}\right|=|k|\,\left|\underset{\sim}{a}\right|$.
$k\underset{\sim}{a}$ is always parallel to $\underset{\sim}{a}$, and $0\underset{\sim}{a}$ is the zero vector $\underset{\sim}{0}$.

foundation.solution_text:
The scalar $\frac{1}{3}$ is positive, so the direction is unchanged.
$\frac{1}{3}\underset{\sim}{c}$ points due east and is one third as long as $\underset{\sim}{c}$.

foundation.question_text: $\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}10\\-15\end{pmatrix}$. Find the value of $k$ for which $\underset{\sim}{b}=k\underset{\sim}{a}$.

development.question_text: $\underset{\sim}{p}=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\6\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{q}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-9\end{pmatrix}$. Find the value of $k$ for which $\underset{\sim}{q}=k\underset{\sim}{p}$.
Explain why $-\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{a}$ is parallel to $\underset{\sim}{a}$ but points the opposite way.
development.solution_text:
$-\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{a}$ is a scalar multiple of $\underset{\sim}{a}$, and every scalar multiple lies along the same line, so the two vectors are parallel.
The scalar $-\frac{1}{2}$ is negative, so the arrow is reversed, and $\left|-\frac{1}{2}\right|=\frac{1}{2}$, so it is half as long.

mastery.question_text: The vector $\underset{\sim}{a}$ has magnitude $6$ and points north-east. State the magnitude and direction of $-\frac{2}{3}\underset{\sim}{a}$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\left|-\frac{2}{3}\underset{\sim}{a}\right|=\frac{2}{3}\times6$
$=4$
The scalar is negative, so the direction is reversed.
$-\frac{2}{3}\underset{\sim}{a}$ has magnitude $4$ and points south-west.
